(men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] | years3 = 2022–2023 | team3 = [[Konyaspor Basketbol|Konyaspor]] | years4 = 2023 | team4 = [[Peristeri B.C.|Peristeri Athens]] | years5 = [[2023 CEBL season|2023]] | team5 = [[Ottawa BlackJacks]] | years6 = 2023–2024 | team6 = [[Dziki Warsaw|Dziki Warszawa]] | years7 = 2024–2025 | team7 = [[Hapoel Haifa B.C.|Hapoel Haifa]] | years8 = 2025–2026 | team8 = [[BC Enisey|Enisey]] | years9 = 2026–present | team9 = [[KK Spartak Subotica|Spartak Subotica]] | highlights = * [[National Invitation Tournament|NIT]] champion ([[2019 National Invitation Tournament|2019]]) * 2× Third-team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] (2020, 2021) * [[Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 tournament]] MOP ([[2021 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|2021]]) | medal_templates = {{MedalSport | Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|the {{bk|USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|FIBA Americas U18 Championship]]}} {{MedalGold| [[2016 FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|2016 Chile]] | [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Clifford Matthew Coleman III''' (born January 22, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[KK Spartak Subotica|Spartak Subotica]] of the [[Basketball League of Serbia|Serbian SuperLeague]], the [[ABA League]], and the [[Basketball Champions League|FIBA Champions League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]]. ==High school career== Coleman played basketball for [[Matthew Fontaine Maury High School]] in [[Norfolk, Virginia]] for two years. After his sophomore season, he transferred to [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] in [[Mouth of Wilson, Virginia]]. As a junior, Coleman helped his team win the High School National title.{{cite web |last1=Rubama |first1=Larry |title=Former Maury basketball star Matt Coleman picks Texas |url=https://www.pilotonline.com/757teamz/basketball/article_069fd4d5-0be0-5a63-9401-d6de928d3d2c.html |website=[[The Virginian-Pilot]] |accessdate=October 28, 2020 |date=January 16, 2017}} He averaged 11.3 points, 7.5 assists, 4.5 rebounds and 2.6 steals per game as a senior, helping Oak Hill finish with a 38–4 record. He was named Virginia [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]].{{cite web |last1=Rubama |first1=Larry |title=Former Maury star Matt Coleman named Gatorade Virginia Player of the Year |url=https://www.pilotonline.com/757teamz/basketball/article_c4b6ecb6-782b-50af-a237-4e06bfd1b1df.html |website=[[The Virginian-Pilot]] |accessdate=October 28, 2020 |date=March 20, 2017}} Coleman played in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and finished with eight points, eights assists and three steals.{{cite web |last1=Moyle |first1=Nick |title=UT commit Matt Coleman put on a show at the Jordan Brand Classic |url=https://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/college_sports/longhorns/article/UT-commit-Matt-Coleman-put-on-a-show-at-the-11074788.php |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |accessdate=October 28, 2020 |date=April 14, 2017}} He was a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to playing college basketball for [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] over an offer from [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], among others. Coleman was drawn by his relationship with coach [[Shaka Smart]]. ==College career== On January 10, 2018, Coleman registered his first career [[double-double]] with 17 points and 12 assists in a 99–98 win over [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]].{{cite web |last1=Winkler |first1=Adam |title=Career-high 12 assists from Norfolk's Matt Coleman propels Texas to emotional upset of No. 16 TCU |url=https://www.wtkr.com/2018/01/11/career-high-12-assists-from-norfolks-matt-coleman-propels-texas-to-emotional-upset-of-no-16-tcu/ |website=[[WTKR]] |accessdate=October 10, 2020 |date=January 11, 2018}} On March 16, he recorded a career-high 25 points and four assists in an 87–83 overtime loss to seventh-seeded [[Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball|Nevada]] in the first round of the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018 NCAA tournament]].{{cite web |last1=Moyle |first1=Nick |title=Texas' Matt Coleman carries hopes for program's future |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/longhorns/article/Texas-Matt-Coleman-carries-hopes-for-program-s-12761602.php |website=[[Houston Chronicle]] |accessdate=October 10, 2020 |date=March 17, 2018}} In his freshman season, he averaged 10.2 points per game, 4.1 assists and 2.5 rebounds per game, earning All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] Honorable Mention.{{cite web |last1=Miller |first1=Andrew |title=Texas Basketball: Matt Coleman primed for huge season with Longhorns in 2018-19 |url=https://hookemheadlines.com/2018/05/07/texas-basketball-matt-coleman-primed-for-huge-season-with-longhorns-in-2018-19/ |website=Hook'em Headlines |accessdate=October 10, 2020 |date=May 7, 2018}} Coleman averaged 9.8 points and 3.4 assists per game as a sophomore, while shooting 38.7 percent from the floor. For a second time, he was selected to the All-Big 12 Honorable Mention.{{cite web |last1=Moyle |first1=Nick |title=Texas needs Matt Coleman and Courtney Ramey to be 'two-headed monster' |url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/college_sports/longhorns/article/Texas-needs-Matt-Coleman-and-Courtney-Ramey-to-be-14477590.php |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |accessdate=October 10, 2020 |date=September 29, 2019}} On November 9, 2019, Coleman posted 22 points and seven assists in a 70–66 victory over [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]].{{cite web |title=Matt Coleman shines as Texas wins at No. 23 Purdue |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2019/11/09/matt-coleman-shines-as-texas-wins-at-no-23-purdue/ |website=[[NBC Sports]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |accessdate=October 10, 2020 |date=November 9, 2019}} As a junior, he averaged 12.7 points, 3.4 assists and three rebounds per game. He was named to the Third Team All-Big 12.{{cite web |last1=Dukes |first1=Chris |title=Texas Basketball: Matt Coleman III Leads Longhorns' All-Big 12 Selections |url=https://www.si.com/college/texas/the-forty-acres/texas-basketball-matt-coleman-iii-leads-longhorns-all-big-12-selections |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |accessdate=October 10, 2020 |date=March 8, 2020}} Coming into his senior season, Coleman was named to the Preseason All-Big 12 Team.{{cite news |last1=Winkler |first1=Adam |title=Norfolk's Matt Coleman voted Preseason All-Big 12 |url=https://www.wtkr.com/sports/norfolks-matt-coleman-voted-preseason-all-big-12 |accessdate=October 29, 2020 |work=WTKR |date=October 28, 2020}} On December 2, 2020, Coleman scored 22 points and hit the game-winning jump shot with 0.1 seconds remaining in a 69–67 win against [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] in the Maui Invitational championship.{{cite news |title=Coleman, No. 17 Texas beat No. 14 UNC 69-67 for Maui title |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401256579 |access-date=December 2, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=December 2, 2020}} On March 13, 2021, he scored 30 points in a 91–86 win over [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]] at the [[2021 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 tournament]] final. He was named tournament most outstanding player.{{cite web |last1=Kosko |first1=Nick |title=Reaction: Matt Coleman steals show as Texas defeats Oklahoma State for Big 12 title |url=https://247sports.com/LongFormArticle/Matt-Coleman-Texas-Oklahoma-State-steals-show-Big-12-championship-reaction-Cade-Cunningham-Shaka-Smart-March-Madness-162370056/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=March 17, 2021 |date=March 13, 2021}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Coleman joined the [[Sacramento Kings]] for the [[2021 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=Kings Announce California Classic Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-announce-2021-ca-classic-roster|work=NBA.com|date=August 1, 2021|access-date=October 3, 2021}} On September 28, 2021, he signed a contract with the Kings.{{cite web|title=Kings Announce 2021-22 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-announce-2021-22-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=September 28, 2021|access-date=September 28, 2021}} He was waived prior to the start of the season. He was later picked up by Sacramento's G League affiliate, the [[Stockton Kings]] as an affiliate player.{{cite web |title=Stockton Kings Announce 2021-22 Training Camp Roster |url=https://stockton.gleague.nba.com/news/stockton-kings-announce-2021-22-training-camp-roster/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 2, 2021 |date=October 25, 2021}} On July 22, 2022, he signed with [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite web|url=https://bjk.com.tr/tr/haber/84119/matt-coleman-besiktasta.html|title=Matt Coleman Beşiktaş'ta|last=|first=|date=July 22, 2022|website=bjk.com.tr|publisher=|language=tr|access-date=August 5, 2022}} On December 9, 2022, he signed with [[Konyaspor (basketball)|AYOS Konyaspor]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketfaul.com/haber?haber=104948|title=Beşiktaş'tan Konyaspor'a|last=|first=|date=December 9, 2022|website=|publisher=basketfaul|language=tr|access-date=December 10, 2022}} On February 8, 2023, Coleman signed with [[Peristeri B.C.|Peristeri Athens]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] for the rest of the season. In 17 domestic Greek league games, he averaged 3.4 points and 1.4 rebounds, while playing around 12 minutes per contest. On June 25, 2023, he parted ways with the Greek club. In June of the same year, Coleman moved to the [[Ottawa BlackJacks]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]].{{cite web|title=Ottawa BlackJacks Sign American Guard Matt Coleman III|url=https://www.cebl.ca/ottawa-blackjacks-sign-american-guard-matt-coleman-iii|work=CEBL.ca|date=May 4, 2023|access-date=June 13, 2023}} On July 13, 2023, Coleman signed with [[Dziki Warszawa]] of the [[Polish Basketball League]].{{cite web|title=Matt Coleman dołącza do watahy!|url=https://www.dziki.basketball/blogs/news/matt-coleman|work=Dziki.basketball|date=July 13, 2023|access-date=October 2, 2023|language=Polish}} On July 17, 2025, Coleman signed a contract with the Russian club [[BC Enisey|Enisey]] of the [[VTB United League]].{{Cite web |title=Мэтт Коулмэн – новый игрок «Енисея»! |url=https://basket-enisey.ru/news/?id=5962}} ==National team career== Coleman represented the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2016 FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]]. He averaged 7.8 points, 4.6 rebounds and 4.4 assists in 22.8 minutes per game, helping his team win the gold medal.{{cite web |title=Men's Basketball signs Matt Coleman to National Letter of Intent |url=https://texassports.com/news/2017/4/12/mens-basketball-signs-matt-coleman-to-national-letter-of-intent.aspx |website=University of Texas Athletics |accessdate=October 28, 2020 |date=April 12,
